newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products--Gulf gasoline up on Lyondell.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products--Gulf gasoline up on Lyondell.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast conventional gasoline differentials rode talk of a shutdown at Lyondell Petrochemical's fluid catalytic cracking unit in Houston to firmer levels Wednesday morning, traders said.
But Lyondell's comments Tuesday that it was restarting the 96,000 barrel per day cracker quickly put a lid on the bullishness the shutdown had generated to begin with.

Activity in other regions was more subdued than in Houston, and the underlying NYMEX market was softer in the wake of bearish inventory reports this week from the Department of Energy and the American Petroleum Institute.

Prompt regular conventional M1 southern grade gasoline was heard done at levels as firm as 3.25 cents under July NYMEX unleaded futures, though that level appeared to be a bit too firm to some traders.
But deals at 3.40 and 3.50 cents under the July print - about 0.50 cent firmer than late Tuesday -- were more confirmable.
Activity on distillates was largely steady compared to Tuesday's levels.
Little movement in the New York Harbor differentials was noted early Wednesday, though players said activity had picked up from the torporic trade seen Tuesday.

Prompt reformulated northern-grade A2 gasoline on the Buckeye Pipeline changed hands at 0.20 and 0.10 cent under the July NYMEX, while offers for barge barrels in the Harbor held steady with yesterday at 0.25 cents under the NYMEX.
"We've seen some bids by a major on the Buckeye barrels," one trader said.
Prompt regular conventional northern-grade M2 gasoline was talked between about 2.50 and 2.60 cents under the July NYMEX, according to market watchers, near unchanged from late Tuesday.
Offers for prompt low sulphur diesel barrels sat between 0.55 and 0.60 cents over the July NYMEX, slightly off the levels seen Tuesday.
Midcontinent products markets were unchanged to slightly weaker from Tuesday morning in very quiet activity, players said. Absolute values, however, were slightly up due to the rise in NYMEX futures.
In Group Three, prompt unleaded gasoline differentials were pegged 4.25/4.75 cents over July NYMEX and any months at 2.80/3.00 cents.
In Chicago markets, prompt unleaded was down a half cent at 3.00/3.25 cents. "With the Merc up and nothing going on it is likely to pressure down differentials," said a products trader.
